newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany joins European shopping mall party -late.
newsitem.headline: Germany joins European shopping mall party -late.

text.p: Europe's largest retail complex opened Thursday in Germany's Ruhr valley offering a "total shopping experience" meant to help transform the economic fortunes of the depressed industrial region.

Built in just two years on the site of an old steelworks, the 2.2 billion mark ($1.45 billion) Centro mall symbolises belated efforts to restructure the ailing German economy -- beset by soaring unemployment and fears its best years are past.
"I hope this project will give a reviving impulse to the whole region, so badly shaken by unemployment," Johannes Rau, North Rhine-Westphalia premier, told an opening ceremony.

Germany is a latecomer to the U.S.-style shopping mall trend which has already peaked elsewhere in western Europe. Many markets are saturated and local officials have tightened planning rules to protect traditional city centres.

The British-built mall in Oberhausen has 220 shops, 50 eateries, nine cinemas, two hotels and an indoor stadium. It has 750,000 square feet of floor space spread over a park of 8.9 million square feet.

Planned to employ 10,000 and billed as Europe's biggest in terms of total area, Centro is still dwarfed by some U.S. malls. Its opening coincides with a mall construction slowdown in other European countries.
